h1: Generators & Surge Protection in Broward County
intro: Protecting a South Florida home from outages and surges takes two layers of defense. A standby generator keeps your essentials running when the grid drops, and whole-home surge protection guards everything on your wiring from voltage spikes. Both depend on the electrical work behind them, so our licensed crew looks at your service in person and gives you one honest price for the layers that fit.

definition.heading: What generators and surge protection do
definition.body: These are the two layers that keep a South Florida home steady through storm season. A generator is backup power that keeps your essentials running when the grid goes down, tied in safely through a transfer switch. Whole-home surge protection installs at your panel and guards your entire system from voltage spikes, not just one device at a time.

symptoms.title: Outages that keep leaving you in the dark
symptoms.body: The power goes out often enough that you have stopped being surprised by it. A generator is how you stop living at the mercy of the grid.

symptoms.title: Medical equipment or a full freezer you cannot lose
symptoms.body: Someone relies on refrigerated medication, or you have a freezer full of food you cannot afford to lose. Backup power is worth having before the next storm season.

symptoms.title: A house full of sensitive electronics
symptoms.body: Televisions, computers, and appliances with circuit boards inside are easy for a single surge to take out at once. Protection at the panel guards all of it from one place.

symptoms.title: You are relying only on power strips
symptoms.body: Plug-in strips protect the one device plugged into them and wear out quietly over time. If they are your only defense, most of your home and its bigger equipment are unprotected.

benefits.title: The essentials stay on
benefits.body: When the grid drops, the power you depend on most keeps running through the outage.

benefits.title: One line of defense for the whole home
benefits.body: A panel-mounted protector guards your entire electrical system from a single point, before surges reach your outlets.

benefits.title: Tied in safely by a licensed crew
benefits.body: A transfer switch keeps generator and grid power separated the way code requires, on grounding we have confirmed is sound.

benefits.title: Peace of mind before the next season
benefits.body: You stop dreading the forecast, knowing your essentials will stay on and your electronics are guarded.

localSections.heading: Heat, humidity, and hurricane season are the reason
localSections.body: South Florida weather is the reason both layers matter. Long hot summers, heavy humidity, and a hurricane season that tests the grid make outages a fact of life, and storms send surges down the line. A generator lives outdoors in heat and salt air, and the grounding surge protection relies on corrodes there, so our installs are built to last.

localSections.heading: Older South Florida homes, service capacity, and grounding
localSections.body: Broward County homes span many eras. An older home's service was sized for its day, not a generator tied into it. Both a generator and surge protection must work with the service and grounding you have, and problem-brand panels or corroded grounds raise questions we answer first. So we pull the permit and meet the inspector, leaving a clean record.

guide.title: The honest guide to storm-season power resilience in South Florida

sections.heading: Two layers: a generator and surge protection
sections.body: Protecting a home down here comes in two parts. The first is losing power: hurricane season tests the grid, and outages can last for days, which is what a generator is for. The second is too much power, too fast: surges are brief voltage spikes that damage electronics, arriving from the grid and from inside your walls. Most homes benefit from both, and we tell you honestly which matters most.

sections.heading: Standby generators and the transfer switch
sections.body: The machine is the easy part. What makes a generator safe is the electrical work that ties it in through a transfer switch, keeping generator and grid power separated. Without it, a generator can backfeed onto the utility lines and injure a lineworker who thinks the line is dead, which is why it is permitted and inspected. For most homes it is about keeping the essentials on, not running everything.

sections.heading: Surge protection, grounding, and choosing an installer
sections.body: Whole-home surge protection installs at your panel and guards the entire system, unlike a plug-in strip that covers one device. It works best on proper grounding, which we confirm before finishing. What a generator can carry is not a brochure number, so both layers are quoted per property after an on-site visit. Choose a licensed installer who pulls a permit and uses an in-house crew, the way our team works.

faqs.question: What can a generator actually run in my home?
faqs.answer: That depends on your electrical service, the install, and the loads you choose to keep on, which is why we assess it in person first. For most homes a generator keeps the essentials alive, the refrigerator, medical equipment, and key systems, rather than running the entire house. We tell you honestly what a setup will and will not carry.

faqs.question: Why does the transfer switch matter so much?
faqs.answer: The transfer switch keeps your home drawing from either the grid or the generator, never both. Without it, a generator can push power back onto the utility lines, injuring a lineworker who thinks the line is dead and damaging your home when grid power returns. It is the component that makes backup power safe, and we never shortcut it.

faqs.question: What does whole-home surge protection actually protect?
faqs.answer: It guards your entire electrical system and everything tied into it, from televisions to appliances with circuit boards inside. Installed at the panel, it stands between your home and surges before they reach your outlets, unlike a plug-in strip that covers only one device. Many surges start inside your own home each time a large motor cycles on, and others arrive from the grid, so protection at the panel addresses the whole picture.

faqs.question: Do you install for commercial properties?
faqs.answer: Yes, for both homes and commercial properties across Broward County. A commercial job raises the same core questions as a home, whether the service can support the system and what has to stay running, just at a larger scale. We assess the property in person and give you one honest price for your specific building.
